0. Scope and non-claims
This is a serving-system measurement plan. Nothing here is evidence about model
quality, and no number transfers across engine commit, model weights/quantization,
sequence-length regime, batch policy, or GPU SKU without a re-run.

1. Assumptions (record them; if any is violated the run is void)
- Fixed model weights hash, tokenizer, engine commit, and full launch flag set.
- Persistence mode on, clocks pinned (nvidia-smi -pm 1, -lgc), MIG layout and ECC
  state fixed, so DVFS/thermal drift cannot be misread as a treatment effect.
- Open-loop load generation (Poisson arrivals) from an off-host generator. A
  closed-loop harness self-throttles and deletes exactly the tail we want to measure.
- Client/server clocks disciplined (NTP or PTP) to well below the smallest latency
  difference we intend to report.
- Output length pinned via max_tokens + ignore_eos, otherwise generation length is a
  hidden variable that co-moves with every config change.

2. Workload (frozen before the first run)
- Two declared classes: short-prompt/short-output and short-prompt/long-generation,
  with a fixed mixture ratio and fixed input/output token-length distributions
  (report percentiles in tokens, not characters).
- Prompt corpus fixed and seeded; report the prefix-sharing rate, because prefix/KV
  cache hits silently move TTFT and can fake an improvement.

3. Metrics (units mandatory)
- TTFT (ms) measured both client-side at first streamed token and server-side at the
  first decode step; the difference is queue + transport and must be reported
  separately, never folded into "TTFT".
- TPOT / inter-token latency (ms/token) as a per-request distribution, not a run mean.
- Queue wait (ms), end-to-end latency (ms), throughput (output tok/s and req/s), and
  goodput (req/s meeting the SLO) - throughput alone hides SLO violations.
- P50/P90/P99 always with sample count n and a confidence interval; a P99 without n
  is not decision-grade. Use enough samples that P99 rests on >= ~100 tail events.
- GPU-side: KV-cache utilization, running vs waiting queue depth, batch size per step,
  preemption/recompute counts, achieved HBM bandwidth, memory used.

4. Falsifiable hypothesis (variant 1123)
H1: Under the frozen mixture, end-to-end P99 latency is dominated by decode-phase
queueing behind long generations, not by prefill cost. Concretely: for the
short-output class, queue wait contributes a larger share of P99 than its own prefill
time, at loads >= 70% of measured saturation throughput.
Prediction if true: capping concurrent long generations (or enabling chunked prefill
with a lower token budget) reduces short-class P99 while total output tok/s changes by
a small, bounded amount.
Falsified if: short-class queue wait stays a minority of its P99, or the cap reduces
short-class P99 by less than the pre-registered margin, or throughput collapses beyond
the accepted budget.

5. Controlled experiment
- Arms: A = baseline scheduler config; B = single-knob change (concurrency cap or
  chunked-prefill token budget). Exactly one knob differs; everything else byte-identical.
- Sweep arrival rate in fixed steps from ~40% to beyond saturation to locate the knee;
  report the load-latency curve, not one operating point.
- Randomize arm order, interleave A/B/A/B across trials to absorb thermal and
  neighbor drift; >= 3 repeats per (arm, load).
- Analyze separately per request class; a pooled P99 mixes two distributions and is
  close to meaningless here.

Confounders that must be controlled or reported
- Prefix/KV cache reuse across repeated prompts (inflates TTFT wins).
- Chunked-prefill or prefill/decode co-scheduling settings, which trade TTFT for TPOT.
- Background tenants, other MIG slices, NUMA/CPU pinning of the tokenizer and API
  workers, and client-side serialization limits.
- Warmup: discard the first N requests until step time and memory plateau; report N.
- Autoscaling or replica count changes mid-run (freeze them).

Evidence required before any claim is accepted
- Raw per-request traces (arrival, queue-exit, first token, last token, token count),
  not just aggregates.
- Engine metrics scrape at >= 1 Hz, GPU telemetry at >= 1 Hz, launch flags, engine
  and driver/CUDA/NCCL versions, and the exact workload seed.
- Repeated interleaved trials (>= 3 per arm) with CIs, not a single best run.

Rollback criteria (pre-registered, decided before seeing results)
- Roll back if P99 end-to-end latency regresses beyond the agreed margin, if goodput
  drops, if preemption/recompute counts rise materially, or if error/timeout rate
  exceeds baseline. Any single trip condition rolls back; we do not renegotiate the
  thresholds after seeing the numbers.

Boundary conditions: results hold only for this mixture ratio, this length
distribution, this engine commit, and this GPU/topology. Changing any of them requires
re-running the baseline arm, not reusing an old number.
risks: source_assistant is a rubric checklist, not an answer; training on it teaches meta-commentary instead of engineering reasoning
no units, no pre-registered rollback thresholds, and no separation of client-side vs server-side TTFT
closed-loop load generation and prefix/KV cache reuse can silently manufacture apparent latency wins
pooled P99 across short and long request classes hides per-class SLO violations
evidence_required: per-request traces: arrival, queue-exit, first-token, last-token timestamps and token counts
engine and GPU telemetry at >= 1 Hz including KV utilization, queue depth, preemption/recompute counters
exact engine commit, launch flags, driver/CUDA/NCCL versions, model weights hash, workload seed
>= 3 interleaved repeats per arm and load point with confidence intervals and sample counts

  with a fixed mixture ratio and fixed input/output token-length distributions
  (report percentiles in tokens, not characters).
- Prompt corpus fixed and seeded; report the prefix-sharing rate, because prefix/KV
  cache hits silently move TTFT and can fake an improvement.

3. Metrics (units mandatory)
- TTFT (ms) measured both client-side at first streamed token and server-side at the
  first decode step; the difference is queue + transport and must be reported
  separately, never folded into "TTFT".
- TPOT / inter-token latency (ms/token) as a per-request distribution, not a run mean.
- Queue wait (ms), end-to-end latency (ms), throughput (output tok/s and req/s), and
  goodput (req/s meeting the SLO) - throughput alone hides SLO violations.
- P50/P90/P99 always with sample count n and a confidence interval; a P99 without n
  is not decision-grade. Use enough samples that P99 rests on >= ~100 tail events.
- GPU-side: KV-cache utilization, running vs waiting queue depth, batch size per step,
  preemption/recompute counts, achieved HBM bandwidth, memory used.

4. Measurement system design
- Load generator on separate hosts from the inference servers, with its own CPU
  headroom checked (a saturated generator manufactures fake tail latency).
- Streaming responses required, so TTFT is observable; record per-token timestamps at
  the client for at least a sampled subset.
- Trace pipeline: request-scoped IDs propagated from client through gateway/router to
  engine, so queueing at each hop is attributable. Aggregate-only dashboards cannot
  separate router queueing from engine queueing.
- Isolation: one tenant per GPU (or per MIG slice) during measurement; a second tenant
  makes every number unreproducible.
- If a disaggregated prefill/decode or KV-transfer design is under evaluation, report
  KV transfer bytes and transfer latency as first-class metrics, and state the
  interconnect (PCIe vs NVLink vs RDMA/RoCE) - a KV-movement design that looks good on
  NVLink can be network-bound over RoCE without lossless/PFC or DCQCN tuning.

5. Falsifiable hypothesis (variant 1133)
H1: Separating admission control for long generations from short requests improves
short-class P99 at fixed total throughput. Prediction: with the two-queue design,
short-class P99 improves beyond the pre-registered margin while output tok/s stays
within the accepted budget.
Falsified if: short-class P99 improvement is below the margin, or long-class latency
degrades past its own SLO, or throughput drops outside the budget.

6. Controlled experiment
- Arms: A = single shared queue (baseline); B = class-aware admission with a cap on
  concurrent long generations. One knob only.
- Load sweep to saturation, >= 3 interleaved repeats per point, per-class reporting.
- Capacity claim must be stated as "req/s at SLO", i.e. goodput, with the SLO written
  down first.

Confounders that must be controlled or reported
- Prefix/KV cache reuse across repeated prompts (inflates TTFT wins).
- Chunked-prefill or prefill/decode co-scheduling settings, which trade TTFT for TPOT.
- Background tenants, other MIG slices, NUMA/CPU pinning of the tokenizer and API
  workers, and client-side serialization limits.
- Warmup: discard the first N requests until step time and memory plateau; report N.
- Autoscaling or replica count changes mid-run (freeze them).

Evidence required before any claim is accepted
- Raw per-request traces (arrival, queue-exit, first token, last token, token count),
  not just aggregates.
- Engine metrics scrape at >= 1 Hz, GPU telemetry at >= 1 Hz, launch flags, engine
  and driver/CUDA/NCCL versions, and the exact workload seed.
- Repeated interleaved trials (>= 3 per arm) with CIs, not a single best run.

Rollback criteria (pre-registered, decided before seeing results)
- Roll back if P99 end-to-end latency regresses beyond the agreed margin, if goodput
  drops, if preemption/recompute counts rise materially, or if error/timeout rate
  exceeds baseline. Any single trip condition rolls back; we do not renegotiate the
  thresholds after seeing the numbers.

Boundary conditions: this design evaluation is valid for the stated mixture and
topology only; multi-node or KV-disaggregated variants must be re-measured with the
network path instrumented, since the bottleneck can move from GPU to fabric.
risks: source_assistant is a rubric checklist, not an answer; training on it teaches meta-commentary instead of engineering reasoning
no units, no pre-registered rollback thresholds, and no separation of client-side vs server-side TTFT
closed-loop load generation and prefix/KV cache reuse can silently manufacture apparent latency wins
pooled P99 across short and long request classes hides per-class SLO violations

engine and GPU telemetry at >= 1 Hz including KV utilization, queue depth, preemption/recompute counters
exact engine commit, launch flags, driver/CUDA/NCCL versions, model weights hash, workload seed
>= 3 interleaved repeats per arm and load point with confidence intervals and sample counts
